attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, said in his own voice and not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: The sarcastic line 'made the mistake of assuming that they'd actually tried' claims the makers made no real efficiency effort. 'Never really tried' reads it fairly. It is a retrospective observation about the named model families.

contract.note: An ordinary plain reading: 'tried' means substantive, implemented efficiency work. The contract does not take it as a literal claim that no one ever researched efficiency, which is fair given that the post admits efficiency teams existed. The contract tests effort, not optimality, so the 'horribly inefficient' judgement has no metric and is not scored.

evidence.note: Meta disclosure from April 2024 describing implemented training-stack changes and a roughly 3x gain in training efficiency for Llama 3. This is concrete, dated efficiency engineering. The size of the gain is self-reported.
Google disclosure from May 2024: Gemini 1.5 Flash was distilled from Pro into a lighter model built to be cheaper to serve. This is an implemented efficiency effort before the post.

OpenAI disclosure from July 2024 of GPT-4o mini, a smaller model, plus an improved shared tokenizer. Weaker evidence, because part of it is about pricing, but it does document engineering for efficiency.

Anthropic disclosure from March 2024: Claude 3 Haiku was built as a compact, fast model within a family designed around speed and cost tradeoffs. Weaker evidence, mostly product positioning, but it shows efficiency-oriented design.

reviews.rationale: The claim that the makers did not actually try to make their models efficient fails the contract. Dated pre-post records from all four named families show implemented efficiency work: Llama 3 training gains, Gemini Flash distillation, GPT-4o mini and its tokenizer, and the compact Claude 3 Haiku. These are company disclosures, but the contract accepts them as proof that the work happened. The 'horribly inefficient' judgement has no metric or comparator, so it is not settled either way.
